name: Sameer Asif
headline: I help early-stage SaaS founders build trust & visibility on LinkedIn, so they can focus on their product | Strategy & execution for real growth.

sections.position: General Member @ KFUEIT Clean and Green Society
sections.bio:
𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗲𝗻𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵. 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿.

Most founders and entrepreneurs pour their heart, mind, and money into creating amazing products, yet when it comes to putting themselves out there on LinkedIn, they freeze.

They wonder:
- “What do I post?”
- “How do I share my journey without sounding salesy?”
- “Will anyone even care?”

Or worse, they think they need fancy ads or viral tricks to get noticed.

But here’s the truth I’ve seen again and again:
- People don’t buy from faceless brands. They buy from humans they trust.
- Especially at the early stage, your biggest asset isn’t just your product, it’s you, the founder.

Your story.
Your vision.
Your values.

The more you show up as a real person, the more you attract the right investors, partners, users, and talent.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗜 𝗵𝗲𝗹𝗽 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲.
I help founders and entrepreneurs turn LinkedIn from an empty profile into a place people actually pay attention to. First, we make sure your profile tells your story clearly, who you are, what you’re building, and why it matters. No corporate jargon, no fluff.

Then, we plan posts that feel real. Honest thoughts, lessons from your journey, insights about your product, so people don’t just scroll past, they connect.
I also show you how to engage with the right people, build trust step by step, and stay visible without spending all day online.

So while you focus on building your company, your LinkedIn quietly builds trust for you in the background.

𝗔 𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗹𝗲 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗺𝗲.
I’m a computer science student, currently developing because my goal is to build my own SaaS product one day.

I know what it feels like to start with an idea and turn it into something real. That’s why I love helping other founders do the same, not just with code, but with clear, human stories that attract the right people.

Right now, my mission is simple: help founders and entrepreneurs build a LinkedIn presence that feels true to them and opens real doors.

If you’re ready to make your profile work for you, 𝗹𝗲𝘁’𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁.
𝗗𝗠 "𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗦𝗧" 𝗮𝗻𝘆𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲. 𝗜’𝗱 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂’𝗿𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝗲𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝗜 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗵𝗲𝗹𝗽.

Today is Sunday. how is everyone feeling. I need your opinion too. wanna talk about it...

A few days ago, I shared how I solved one of the biggest problems I was facing as a freelancer in Pakistan:

Receiving international payments.

That post was about discovering a solution.

But after using it, I realized there was a bigger lesson behind it.

People don't always need more motivation.

Sometimes they just need less friction.

For months, the payment question was sitting somewhere in the back of my mind.

“What if I get an international client?”
“How will I receive the payment?”
“What documents will I need?”
“Will the verification process be complicated?”

These questions create hesitation.
And hesitation delays action.

Once I found a simple solution and experienced a relatively quick onboarding process, the problem suddenly felt much smaller.

now I have multiple option for payments direct to USD and Bank accounts.
I will share all of these option with all of you too

That got me thinking about SaaS founders.

You can have an amazing product.

You can have a great LinkedIn presence.

You can create valuable content.

You can explain your product perfectly.

But if there is too much friction between:

“I am interested” ---> “I want to try this”

people can still walk away.

Maybe your signup process is complicated.
Maybe your messaging isn't clear.

Maybe prospects don't understand what happens after they book a call.
Maybe your onboarding asks for too much too early.
Maybe your content creates interest but doesn't make the next step obvious.

These small things can become big barriers. That is the core problem.

And this is something I keep learning as I build my own personal brand too because in this age we need continously improvements.

Don't just convince people to take action.

Make taking that action easier.

For example, a SaaS product shouldn't just say “Book a demo”  it could say “See how we can save your team 5+ hours every week ----> book a 15-minute demo.” 

see that makes a lot of difference. and that is what needed

That's one of the things I look for when helping SaaS founders with their LinkedIn presence.

Because good content isn't only about getting attention.

It should reduce uncertainty, build trust, and make the next step feel natural.

Sometimes growth doesn't require adding more.
Sometimes you just need to remove what's stopping people.

If you're a SaaS founder and you're creating content on LinkedIn but it's not turning into conversations or leads, maybe the problem isn't your product. It might be the friction in your content.

Send me a DM. and I will take a look at your LinkedIn content and point out one thing you can improve to make it easier for the right prospects to take the next step.

No pitch. Just one actionable improvement you can use.

Don't waste more time it is already too late....fire dm nowwwww

More than 650 followers. 🎉

A small number on the screen, but a meaningful milestone for me.

When I started showing up on LinkedIn, I wasn’t sure where this journey would take me. 

I did not even know what LinkedIn was. If I look back at that time I laugh at myself I just throw facebook strategy and post directly into LinkedIn. By Imagine the awkward moment..ahhhhh

I took several breaks from LinkedIn some of two months some of three but one thing I did not quit. I was contantly reading post on Linkedin and soomtimes ocassionally engaging. 

Then I had a powerfull momentum, get full throttle made content plan and yesssss I started from 0 to 1000 impressions.

I just knew I wanted to:
→ share what I’m learning
→ connect with like-minded people
→ provide value through my content
→ build something meaningful over time

And guess what LinkedIn gave a special surprise for my efforts.

Boooom

"Your account has been restricted due to violations"
for what 😭 😭😭😭
long story short (I'll explain it another time) I got my account back 1.5 months later and all efforts reached to zero. but I started once again later on

And now, 650 people have chosen to follow along after this much effort.

To everyone who has liked, commented, shared, connected, or simply read one of my posts:

Thank you. 🤝

I’m grateful for every bit of support.

But I also know this is just the beginning.

More lessons.
More experiments.
More value.
More growth.

The goal isn’t just to reach a bigger number.
It’s to build a community where people can learn, connect, and grow together.

650 today. Let’s see where this journey takes us next. 

Thank you for being part of it.

Congratulations to my Muslim community on Day of 12 Rabi ul Awal

12 Rabi ul Awal is not just a date on the calendar.

For me, it is a day to pause, remember, and reflect on the life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ a life that continues to teach the world about truth, mercy, patience, humility, and character.

I celebrate this day because remembering the Prophet ﷺ is not only about knowing his story.

It is about asking ourselves:

What can I learn from his life, and how can I bring those lessons into mine?

And I’m sharing this on LinkedIn because these values are not limited to one part of our lives.

LinkedIn is a place where we talk about careers, businesses, leadership, success, personal branding, and growth.

But behind all of these things is ""character"".

How we treat our colleagues.

How we speak to people who cannot benefit us.

How we respond when we are angry.

How we handle success.

How we behave when nobody is watching.

These things matter just as much as our professional achievements.

The life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reminds us to:

→ Speak the truth, even when it is difficult.
→ Keep our promises.
→ Treat people with kindness and dignity.
→ Be patient during difficult times.
→ Forgive when we have the ability to hold a grudge.
→ Remain humble when we succeed.
→ Help others without always expecting something in return.

We often ask:

-- How can I become more successful?

Maybe we should also ask:

-- How can I become a better human being?

Because success can give us a position.

-- But character determines what we do with that position.

So today, I’m not only celebrating a significant day.

I’m taking it as a reminder to learn, reflect, and improve through my actions. Beacuse thoes teachings reflect our whole life and only by applying those we can achieve great success

May Allah help us understand the teachings of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and reflect them in our everyday lives.

“The best of you are those who are best in character.”by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

12 Rabi ul Awal Mubarak. 🤍

Most people are constantly waiting on LinkedIn ...
And for what (yes...including you)

- How can I build my presence ?
- How can I be more Authentic?
- How can I build my audience?
- How can I build my business?
- How can I build my visiblity?
- How can I get more engagement?
- How can I close deals with clients?
- How can I earn money?

The last question is the one most people don't want to talk about... but I will be fair and square 

--- Almost everyone want to earn from what they are building ---
 
And there is nothing wrong with that (It is completely normal)

We want our content to attract opportunities.
We want our profiles to bring conversations.
we want our audience to build a community 
we want your community to build customers.
we want our work to create an income

This is business
This is normal
This is nature of human

Look at people who build build businesses, communities, audiences and opportunities through LinkedIn Justin Welsh, Sahil Bloom, Jasmin Alić, Lara Acosta, Alex Hormozi, Charlie Hills 🦩, Ayesha Ameer, Sana Arif 🇵🇰, Fahad Nasir, Matt Barker, Mahdi Shafiei, Marina Panova, Alicia Teltz, Ibtehaj Ahmed

This is just a list people (a very shortlisted one)

They consistently created
They shared ideas
They build trust
They showed up
They comminicated what they know

AND the most important thing, they kept going when nobody was watching...

That is also the stage where most people get stuck, lost confidence, lost energy and momentum which could be their final break thorugh..

They want results. They don't want process
They want personal brands but don't want to write
They want audience but don't want to communicate
They want authority but don't want to share what they know
They want their profile to convert but don't want to spend time understanding who they are talking to.

AND they expect someone else to come along and say:

I'll do the work for you.
I'll build your brand.
I'll write your post
I'll revamp your profile
I'll fix your postining
I'll turn your ideas into content
I'll  make sure people understand what your actually do

So, YESSSSS... people like me exist who will boldy say and want you to understand:

someone can help you write
someone can help you turn your thoughts into posts
someone can help you months of trials and error

but you still have to care about the outcome
LinkedIn is a vending machine nor a magic staff:

you write 10 posts and get 5 clients
you optimized your headline and make a million dollar business
you post for 10 days and get unbreakable authority

It takes patience and learning.
nobody wants to be a begineer
but remaining beginner is your choice

I Help SaaS founders turn their ideas and expertise into posts which build brands and start conversations 

While your work will be foucsing on business

The next I write can be yours. Stop waiting and DM me know to start building the way you want
